paper.title_en: Evaporation residue cross sections for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>170</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>172</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reactions: Sub-barrier fusion enhancement and the role of hexadecapole deformation
paper.abstract_en:
Background: The role of hexadecapole deformation (<math><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math>) in sub-barrier fusion has been studied for the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>174</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>176</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reactions; however, the extracted <math><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> values are model dependent and carry systematic uncertainties that remain unresolved.
Purpose: We extend fusion cross-section measurements to the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>170</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>172</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reactions to investigate isotopic dependence of fusion excitation functions and to clarify the role of higher-order static deformations across the complete <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>170</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>172</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>174</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>176</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> isotopic chain.
Method: Evaporation residue (ER) cross sections for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>170</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>172</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> were measured from 12% below to 35% above the Coulomb barrier using the Heavy Ion Reaction Analyzer (HIRA) at IUAC, New Delhi. The data are analyzed within the coupled-channels and statistical model frameworks.
Results: A strong sub-barrier fusion enhancement is observed relative to one-dimensional barrier penetration model (1D-BPM) predictions. Coupled-channels calculations incorporating quadrupole and hexadecapole deformations of the target nuclei reproduce the measured fusion excitation functions for both reactions. Statistical model calculations with a single fission-barrier scaling factor <math><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow></math> reproduce the ER and fission cross sections simultaneously, over the entire measured energy range. The single-Gaussian barrier-distribution analysis shows that <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>174</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> exhibits the largest sub-barrier enhancement among the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>170</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>172</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>174</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>176</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></math> nuclei.
Conclusions: Coupled-channels calculations including both quadrupole <math><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and hexadecapole <math><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> deformations of the target nuclei successfully reproduce the measured fusion excitation functions for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>170</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>172</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>. Our analysis brings out the role of <math><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> across the entire range of Yb nuclei. The reproduction of ER and fission excitation functions with <math><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow></math> rules out noncompound nuclear fission (NCNF) contributions for both systems. The pronounced sub-barrier enhancement in <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>174</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> is attributed to the midshell character of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>174</mn></mmultiscripts></math> (<math><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> = 104), where nuclear collectivity is maximal.
